taxonomy:
# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Games

## I. Path & Connection Puzzles
Games where solvers trace or connect routes through the grid.

### A. Closed Loop Puzzles
Puzzles requiring a single continuous loop.
- Dotchi-Loop
- Masyu
- Mid-loop
- Slitherlink

### B. Open Path Puzzles
Puzzles with paths that don't form closed loops.
- Hashiwokakeru (bridge connections)
- Numberlink
- Suraromu

### C. Chain Puzzles
Puzzles involving chained or connected pieces.
- Chained Block
- Hebi

## II. Coloring & Marking Puzzles
Games where cells are marked with specific colors or states.

### A. Binary State (Marked/Unmarked)
- Akari (lit/unlit)
- Hitori (marked/unmarked cells)
- Heyawake
- Kurodoko
- Kurotto
- Nagareru
- Nurimeizu
- Nurimisaki
- Satogaeri
- Sto-stone
- Tilepaint

### B. Multi-State Coloring
- Norinori (three colors)
- Ripple Effect (multi-color regions)
- Shakashaka (triangular coloring)
- Usowan

## III. Polyomino Placement Puzzles
Games where polyominoes or shaped pieces are placed on the grid.

### A. Standard Polyomino Puzzles
- Fillomino
- Five Cells
- LITS
- Shikaku

### B. Variant Polyomino Puzzles
- Choco Banana
- Double Choco
- Evolomino
- Makaro
- Moon-or-Sun
- Nurikabe
- Nuritwin
- Yosenabe

## IV. Region & Boundary Puzzles
Games focusing on dividing grids into regions with specific properties.

### A. Line-Drawing Region Puzzles
- Sashigane
- Yajilin

### B. Clue-Based Region Puzzles
- Juosan
- Nansuke
- Pencils

## V. Hybrid & Complex Puzzles
Games combining multiple puzzle mechanics.

- Makaro (polyomino + coloring)
- Suraromu (path + number constraints)

## VI. Logic & Constraint Puzzles
Games primarily based on logical deduction and constraints.

### A. Elimination & Uniqueness
- Hitori
- Sudoku

### B. Property-Based Logic
- Yajilin
- Ripple Effect

---

**Note:** Some games could reasonably fit into multiple categories. This taxonomy prioritizes primary mechanics while acknowledging the hybrid nature of several puzzles.
